job.title: Host Family Provider
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Contract: Temporary engagement

Location: Within three miles (15 minutes), easy access to The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Working Arrangements: Remote

Closing Date For Applications: INSERT

About the Role:

We are recruiting for host families who can provide accommodation for our Academy players to support them living away from home. This is a unique and rewarding opportunity to make a real difference to their experience and provide vital support to the players as they develop as young people alongside their football.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Provide a homely and friendly environment for our young people

  • Support with the development of our young people in your care with their independent living and self-care skills

  • Include our young people in family life as much as they feel comfortable with

  • Provide access to a private bedroom, bathroom, laundry facilities, and communal areas of the house

  • Provide a nutritious evening meal 

  • Report any welfare concerns to the Safeguarding and Welfare team should they occur.

  • Allow access from the Club for regular inspection and visits throughout the season.

  • Adhere to any further and ongoing requirements of Host Families, as outlined in the application process, guidance will be provided by the Club on this. 

What are we looking for:

  • Provide a warm, welcoming and safe environment for our young person

  • Provide the young person with their own private bedroom and relevant amenities 

  • Excellent communication and listening skills

  • Ability to cope with the young person's flexible schedule throughout the football season

  • Previous experience of working with young people

  • Ability to promote and demonstrate anti-discriminatory practice 

As part of the recruitment process the Club would need to conduct a number of home visits to determine suitability and ensure the home meets the requirements for hosting young people within the Academy.

Forest For Everyone

At Nottingham Forest Football Club we are committed to creating an environment where differences are respected, individuality is celebrated, everyone feels valued, supported, and included. Our goal is to ensure every member of our team can be themselves, contribute fully, and reach their potential without barriers.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion and Mental Wellbeing

As an equal opportunities employer, we welcome applications from talented people of all backgrounds regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We continue to develop policies and practices that promote equality, diversity, inclusion and mental wellbeing across our workforce. To help us measure progress and hold ourselves accountable, we ask all applicants to provide accurate diversity information during the recruitment process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check or an enhanced DBS check. The results of a DBS check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act in a proportionate manner when deciding whether or not to proceed with the appointment.

An FA Enhanced DBS disclosure is required for all relevant new appointments to the Club. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions or reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that may have been incurred. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed on a DBS disclosure if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements. Failure to satisfy the Club and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment.

Health and Safety

At Nottingham Forest Football Club, we are committed to ensuring a safe and healthy working environment for all employees. In accordance with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, you are required to take reasonable care for your own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by your actions or omissions at work. You must also cooperate with the Club's health and safety policies and procedures. Should you identify any health and safety concerns, please report them promptly to your manager or a member of the Health and Safety/Facilities team.

job.title: PDP Physiotherapist
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Academy Sports Science and Medical

Reporting to: Head of Academy Physiotherapy

Closing Date For Applications: 6th November 2026

About the Role:

This post is expected to involve contributing significantly to both the Medical and Performance departments to optimise the availability and enhance the long-term athletic development of Nottingham Forest Academy players through optimal service provision in the medical department. The role will require the individual to assist in the medical management, co-ordination and supervision of the of the PDP players, including all aspects of medical screening, injury assessment, diagnosis, management and prevention strategies in line with evidence-based practice. To assist the Head of Academy Physiotherapy in the day-to-day running of the medical department, working as a mentor for the junior staff.

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

Management of Injuries:

  • To primarily work with the B Team squad providing physiotherapy services.

  • To lead on the treatment and management of injuries sustained to players in the PDP squads, working closely with the performance staff to co-ordinate and deliver evidence and performance-based rehab programmes.

  • To standardise the management of injuries by assisting in the development and structure of injury rehabilitation protocols and philosophy.

  • To monitor the effectiveness of injury management principles through clinical injury audits and training availability.

  • To ensure effective, appropriate and thorough communication of injury updates are provided to the player, coaching staff and other relevant staff members.

  • To assist the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy in the provision of physiotherapy services across all age groups and to help oversee the use of part time physiotherapists and sports therapists in their provision of medical care to all players in the Academy.

Injury Prevention:

  • To provide musculoskeletal screening/profiling for all Academy players and integrate this with the Club medical records.

  • To lead the musculoskeletal screening/profiling for PDP players and assist with the process for all Academy players and integrate this with the Club medical records.

  • To work alongside the performance staff to deliver individualised effective injury prevention strategies in both individual and group sessions.

  • To liaise effectively with the Academy coaching staff on a daily basis to keep them informed of players’ availability for Academy matches and training.

  • To work alongside the performance staff to deliver first class recovery and injury prevention strategies to all players both immediately after games and on recovery days.

  • To ensure all players are educated on the importance of recovery, health and athletic development.

Pre-Signing Medicals & Medical Consultations:

  • To assist co-ordinate the pre-signing medical assessments of all Academy players and trialist as required including the writing of formalised pre-signing medical reports.

  • To assist the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy in escalating clinical cases for imaging and/or consultant referrals.

  • To accompany players to medical consultations at short notice either in this country or abroad. Ensuring best practice is always followed and ensuring the player receives optimal care and advice, providing clinical handovers pre and post appointment.

  • To assist the Academy Doctor in co-ordinating the cardiac screening for the PDP squads in line with FA regulations.

  • To manage the FA whereabouts schedule for the PDP squads and assist with the education of players regarding their anti-doping responsibilities.

Medical Provision at Matches/Training Sessions/Tours:

  • To provide physiotherapy match day cover for B Team games and assist other age groups when needed.

  • To assist in organisation and implementation of the medical provision for all training camps for the PDP squads as required.

  • To ensure all medical equipment and procedures are regularly reviewed and maintained at the training ground and at all training and match venues under the guidance of the Head of Academy Physiotherapy.

Management Responsibilities:

  • To take an active role in all medical meetings, MDT meetings and other planning meetings.

  • To take a mentoring role within the department, working as a mentor for junior physiotherapists and being pro-active with assisting CPD for the part time physiotherapists.

  • To assist in the production of an injury audit on a monthly and annual basis for the Academy and feedback to provide accountability for the department and actively seek to follow best practice.

  • To ensure appointments are made for consultations and appropriate travel arrangements made for all Academy players as required, ensuring the 1st Team Medical Department are notified in advance to manage the Club’s Health Partners insurance scheme.

CPD:

  • To assist with delivery and organisation of in-service training sessions in conjunction with the Head of Academy Performance & Medical and Head of Academy Physiotherapy, including the creation of a CPD department pathway to ensure the on-going development of knowledge and skills.

  • To take responsibility for continued professional development to ensure regular attendance of appropriate courses, conferences and keep an up-to-date file of CPD achievements, feeding back any relevant learning points to the department.

Professional Standards:

  • To produce daily reports of injured development players, ensuring all medical notes are up to date within 24 hours of treatment and in line with CSP core standards.

  • To ensure all medical documents are maintained in line with information governance principles.

  • To work with the Safeguarding team to highlight cases for attention through the appropriate channels as required and ensure all relevant training qualifications are maintained.

  • To always maintain a flexible approach to work, including the requirement to undertake other duties and responsibilities as required from time to time.

  • To keep confidential any information gained regarding the charity, Club and its personnel.

  • To ensure compliance with all relevant Club policies, including health and safety policies.

  • To always support Nottingham Forest FC in their aims and objectives.

  • To always represent Nottingham Forest FC in a professional manner.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • BSc (Hons) Physiotherapy or higher degree

  • Member of the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC)

  • Member of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapists (MCSP)

  • Valid ATMMiF Qualification

  • Indemnity through professional registration to £5 million liability

  • Minimum of 2 years post qualification experience

  • Experience of working within a multidisciplinary team

  • Sports Medicine environment preferably with younger athletes

  • Excellent clinical reasoning and manual therapy skills

  • Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills

  • Excellent range of clinical treatment skills an emphasis on rehabilitation

  • Excellence in the understanding and delivery of rehabilitation

  • Medicine from plinth to pitch

  • Management skills to manage a multidisciplinary group of part time practitioners within the Academy Medicine department

  • Set and maintain high standards of work performance and deliver quality consistently and effectively

  • A good understanding of the principles of human performance and how they relate to clinical sports medicine

  • A learning pathway showing the development of a strong evolving clinical paradigm in the field of Physiotherapy (minimum of 36 hours CPD annually to maintain professional registration)

  • Good knowledge of injury screening, diagnostics, manual therapy, injury prevention and recovery strategies

  • Ability to lead group sessions and deliver gym and pitch-based programmes to groups and individuals particularly to adolescents

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills that are clear, engaging and responsive to convey complex information

  • Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing demands and deadlines

  • Hold a full current up to date driving licence

  • Proactive and engaging style with a winning attitude and co-do approach. Flexible approach and attitude to working hours

  • Highest standards of professionalism and personal conduct – especially around the issue of confidentiality

  • Long term commitment to working within a multi-disciplinary medical team

Desirable:

  • Higher (MSc) Sports Medicine Degree

  • Sports Science Diploma/Degree

  • UKSCA/strength and conditioning qualifications

  • Playing experience to a high level

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer.  We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions.  If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below.  The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

Health and Safety

Nottingham Forest is committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees, contractors, visitors, and guests. All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

- BSc (Hons) Physiotherapy or higher degree - Member of the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) - Member of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapists (MCSP) - Valid ATMMiF Qualification - Indemnity through professional registration to £5 million liability - Minimum of 2 years post qualification experience - Experience of working within a multidisciplinary team - Sports Medicine environment preferably with younger athletes - Excellent clinical reasoning and manual therapy skills - Excellent problem solving and decision-making skills - Excellent range of clinical treatment skills an emphasis on rehabilitation - Excellence in the understanding and delivery of rehabilitation - Medicine from plinth to pitch - Management skills to manage a multidisciplinary group of part time practitioners within the Academy Medicine department - Set and maintain high standards of work performance and deliver quality consistently and effectively - A good understanding of the principles of human performance and how they relate to clinical sports medicine - A learning pathway showing the development of a strong evolving clinical paradigm in the field of Physiotherapy (minimum of 36 hours CPD annually to maintain professional registration) - Good knowledge of injury screening, diagnostics, manual therapy, injury prevention and recovery strategies - Ability to lead group sessions and deliver gym and pitch-based programmes to groups and individuals particularly to adolescents - Excellent written and verbal communication skills that are clear, engaging and responsive to convey complex information - Exceptional organisational skills with the ability to manage competing demands and deadlines - Hold a full current up to date driving licence - Proactive and engaging style with a winning attitude and co-do approach. Flexible approach and attitude to working hours - Highest standards of professionalism and personal conduct – especially around the issue of confidentiality - Long term commitment to working within a multi-disciplinary medical team

- Higher (MSc) Sports Medicine Degree - Sports Science Diploma/Degree - UKSCA/strength and conditioning qualifications - Playing experience to a high level

job.title: Safety Steward (Casual)
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

The primary role is to provide a high level of care and comfort and wellbeing of all persons attending the event and to provide a direct and ongoing interaction between them and the grounds Safety Management Team. Stewards should present themselves in a positive, courteous and professional manner at all times, and be focused on maximising every opportunity to enhance the customer experince.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as directed by the Stewarding Services Lead

  • Not to leave the stadium after registering your attendance until completion of your duties as directed by the Safety Management Team

  • Attend pre-event briefings and ensure all information is understood and what your role entails as well as your areas of responsibility

  • To be responsible for the safety, care, comfort, and well-being of spectators within a designated area at all times

  • Remain at allocated post as instructed unless authorised or ordered to do otherwise by a Supervisor or a member of the Safety Management Team

  • Assist spectators in locating their seats by active engagement and ticket checks

  • Prevent overcrowding by ensuring crowd limits for your area of responsibility are complied with

  • Ensure gangways, vomitories, exits and evacuation routes always remain clear of persons and obstructions

  • Where necessary assist in diverting spectators to other areas of the ground to prevent overcrowding

  • Immediately report to a Supervisor, Head Steward or a member of the Safety Management Team, occurrences of persons climbing gates, fences, external walls or other structures within the confines or the perimeter of the ground

  • Monitor the crowd for signs of distress or overcrowding and act in accordance with Club procedures

  • Identify and investigate any incident or occurrence amongst spectators and report your findings to a Supervisor

  • Be aware of the location of, and if suitably trained, be able to operate fire-fighting equipment effectively

  • Be aware of locations of first aid rooms and other first aid equipment retained elsewhere in the Stadium

  • Be willing to be trained in basic lifesaving skills

  • Be fully conversant with any methods/messages or signals used to alert staff that an emergency has arisen

  • Be capable of recognising potential fire hazards and suspect packages, reporting such findings immediately to a Supervisor or a member of the Safety Management Team

  • To carry out all instructions given by the Safety Officer, through the management structure and to promptly comply with any instruction given in an emergency by a Police Officer

  • Report to a supervisor any damage, defect or hazard which is likely to pose a threat to spectator safety e.g. a damaged seat, debris or hazardous substance

What are we looking for:

  • Stewards should be fit, active and not less than age l8 years of age.

  • Have the ability to work on own initiative and as part of a team.

  • To remain calm and efficient and be able to work under pressure.

  • Have a polite and courteous manner.

  • Be able to adapt to different and changing situations.

  • Be flexible to work in different locations and roles within Stadium.

  • Be of smart appearance and personal hygiene with good communication skills.

  • Help to manage conflict and demonstrate confidence to challenge inappropriate behaviour.

  • Be able to remain stationary for prolonged periods, either standing or seated, climb and descend stairs.

  • Have basic numeracy and literacy skills

  • Be willing to undertake and complete level 2 Certificate in Spectator Safety.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. job.title: Corporate Steward (Casual)
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

The Corporate Security Team Member will be responsible for supporting all aspects of security operations within the hospitality areas of Nottingham Forest Football Club. This includes following security policies and procedures, assisting with managing access control, and ensuring the safety of all club assets, employees, and visitors. The ideal candidate will have a background in security, excellent observation skills, and a proactive approach to ensuring safety.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Monitor and patrol hospitality areas, including VIP areas, lounges, and dining facilities.

  • Enforce security policies and procedures to ensure a safe environment.

  • Assist with managing access control, including checking tickets and guest lists.

  • Provide security support during all hospitality events, including match days, private functions, and special events.

  • Coordinate with event management teams to ensure the safety of guests, staff, and VIPs.

  • Assist with crowd control and ensure orderly conduct of guests.

  • Respond promptly to security incidents and emergencies within hospitality areas.

  • Assist with the resolution of incidents, ensuring a safe and effective outcome.

  • Report incidents to the Hospitality Security Manager and assist with incident documentation.

  • Provide excellent customer service to guests, staff, and VIPs.

  • Assist guests with inquiries and directions, maintaining a helpful and professional demeanour.

  • Promote a culture of security awareness among guests and staff.

  • Ensure compliance with all relevant legal and regulatory requirements related to hospitality security.

  • Maintain accurate records of security activities and incidents.

  • Assist with the preparation of security reports for senior management

What are we looking for:

  • Previous experience in security, preferably within a hospitality or sports environment.

  • Knowledge of security systems and procedures.

  • Strong observational and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and in emergency situations.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Relevant security certifications (e.g., SIA license) preferable.

job.title: Turnstile Operator (Casual)
job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

The purpose of this role is to ensure the safe, efficient and welcoming entry of supporters into the stadium on matchdays and during events. You will be responsible for managing access through stadium turnstiles, accurately checking and validating tickets, passes and other relevant entry credentials, and ensuring that only authorised individuals gain access to the stadium.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Operating turnstiles or scanning electronic tickets at stadium entrances

  • Checking tickets, season cards, and accreditation passes for validity

  • Assisting supporters with entry issues (e.g., invalid tickets, scanning errors)

  • Providing directions and basic information to fans entering the stadium

  • Maintaining orderly queues and managing crowd flow at entry points

  • Ensuring entry procedures comply with stadium safety and security policies

  • Reporting suspicious behaviour, incidents, or safety concerns to supervisors

  • Supporting emergency procedures if required (e.g., evacuation instructions)

  • Delivering a polite, professional, and customer-focused service at all times

What are we looking for:

  • Friendly, calm, and confident when dealing with large crowds

  • Good communication and customer service skills

  • Ability to remain alert and focused in a busy environment

  • Comfortable standing for long periods outdoors in all weather conditions

  • Able to follow instructions and safety procedures strictly

  • Team player, working closely with other stewards and supervisors

job.location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ, GB
job.html_description:
Engagement: Casual position offering variable hours on a flexible basis

Location: The City Ground, Nottingham, NG2 5FJ

Department: Safety and Security

Reporting to: Safety Officer

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

To provide support and assistance in managing Safeguarding, Accessibility and Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) incidents at The City Ground on matchdays. This includes responding to concerns raised by supporters, offering appropriate guidance and support, and ensuring any incidents are handled sensitively, professionally and in line with Club policies and procedures. The role will help promote a safe, inclusive and welcoming matchday environment for all supporters, ensuring that any concerns are appropriately recorded, escalated and followed up where necessary.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Assist the Club in the effective, safe customer friendly management of matchdays and event days at the City Ground

  • Work in any area of the Stadium as directed by the Ground Safety Officer, Deputy Safety Officer or Stand Supervisor.

  • Attend Safeguarding, Accessibility or EDI related incidents within your designated location and resolve wherever possible, providing updates to the control room and completed incident reports post event.

  • Liaise with relevant departments relating to incidents where required.

  • Assist with supplying details in the event of an incident.

  • Assisting supporters with Accessibility requirements.

  • Ensure the radial gangway is kept clear.

  • Identify and report any potential safety issues.

  • Ensuring that the supervisor or relevant senior member of staff is alerted with appropriate information given.

  • Being a direct link between Safeguarding, EDI and match-day staff.

  • Assist with providing Supporter details to the Police upon request in line with our GDPR ‘data sharing agreement’.

  • To work consistently to embed and champion safeguarding, equality & diversity into the match-day experience.

  • Promote an inclusive, positive, supportive, and welcoming image of the club at all times.

  • Ensure compliance with the terms of the Club Safeguarding Policies and Procedures, Health and Safety Legislation and Club’s Equality Policy.

  • Support accessibility and inclusion on match days including accessible areas and multi-faith rooms.

  • Attend and respond to briefing and debriefing in relation to safety management and to report any matters of concern or interest to the Stand Supervisor Steward.

  • To undertake internal and/or external training including stewarding, Safeguarding, accessibility and EDI training required for the role as directed by the Club.

  • Any other reasonable duties and responsibilities which your manager or another senior officer of the Club asks you to perform.

What are we looking for:

  • Willingness to work in crowd management in a football environment

  • Good communication skills

  • Ability to deliver and maintain high levels of customer service

  • Knowledge and Experience around Safeguarding, Accessibility, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion.

  • Experience working within a Sporting Stadium

  • Previous Safeguarding experience with children and/or adults at risk

Forest For Everyone

We aim to create a culture which embraces and celebrates our differences, enables individuals to feel comfortable, maximise their potential and eliminate discrimination.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified persons, regardless of age, disability, gender, gender reassignment, marital / civil partnership status, pregnancy / maternity leave, race, religion/belief, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Nottingham Forest Football Club is a signatory of the FA’s Football Leadership Diversity Code. We are committed to developing policies to promote equal opportunities and diversity within our workforce. To monitor our progress against these commitments, we Invite all applicants to provide diversity data during the application process.

Disability Confident Committed Employer

We are a Disability Confident Committed employer. We encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a "disabled person" according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment selections.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

As part of the Club’s commitment to safeguarding, the successful applicant may be required to undergo a Disclosure Barring Service (“DBS”) check. The level of check required will depend on the requirements of the role. Individuals will be asked to declare any convictions, cautions, reprimands, warnings or bind-overs that they are required to disclose for the level of check applicable to the role, in accordance with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (as amended) and the DBS filtering rules. The results of any check will be considered on an individual basis, and the Club will act proportionately in deciding whether to proceed with the appointment. The Club reserves the right to carry out risk assessments where content has been disclosed if it feels that it is relevant to the job requirements of the role. Failure to satisfy the Club, FA’s and the PL's safeguarding requirements may lead to the job offer being withdrawn or, if they have already started employment, summary termination of the employment, in accordance with the Club's disciplinary procedures

Health and Safety

Nottingham Forest is committed to maintaining a safe and healthy working environment for all employees, contractors, visitors, and guests. All employees are expected to comply with company health and safety policies, procedures and risk assessments, use equipment and PPE correctly and report any hazards, accidents and near misses. Appropriate training will be provided to ensure everyone understands their health and safety responsibilities.

job.title: Women's Physiotherapist
job.location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR, GB
job.html_description:
Salary: Please state your expectations within your application

Contract: Full Time, 42 hours a week

Location: The Nigel Doughty Academy, Nottingham, NG2 7SR

Department: Forest Women

Closing Date For Applications: 16th November 2026

About the Role:

Will be responsible for injury mitigation strategies, the rehabilitation of player and pitch side provision for training and matchdays

The Perks of the Job:

  • Opportunity to access tickets for events at The City Ground.

  • Employee Assistance Programme.

  • Access to high street and gym discounts.

  • Discount within our Club shop.

  • Free on-site parking.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

  • Provide high quality provision for Nottingham Forest Women first team players, ensuring full assessment and diagnosis.

  • Plan and oversee the treatment and rehabilitation of injured players, ensuring injuries are managed to meet professional standards.

  • Ensure all injuries are documented appropriately, escalated where appropriate and the necessary evaluations are done to ensure any learnings are made.

  • To liaise with coaching staff to support the load management of players and return to play pathway for injured athletes.

  • Provide effective communication throughout the multi-disciplinary team, ensuring all updates are communicated to all relevant parties.

  • Work with the MDT to support the delivery of injury prevention programmes.

  • Provide pitch side cover for all training and matches (home and away).

  • To liaise with internal (Club Doctor, medical team) and external (NHS/Private) stakeholders to facilitate external medical management, where necessary.

  • Work with the Head of Women’s and Girls to continue to develop the player care/support strategy.

  • To support a performance-based culture which maximises players potential through prevention, treatment and education.

  • Always ensure appropriate professional confidentiality and behave at all times to project a professional image of Nottingham Forest FC and act in the Club’s best interests.

  • Ad hoc duties required by the Head of Women and Girls Football to meet the needs of the business.

What are we looking for:

Essential:

  • BSc in Physiotherapy/Sports Rehabilitation/Therapy or equivalent

  • HCPC or BASRaT Membership

  • Pitch side qualification; ITMMiF (essential), ATMMiF (desirable)

  • Appropriate medical indemnity (and insurance) to treat and advise players

  • At least 1 years practical experience working in an elite sport environment

  • Confident communicator at all levels

  • A good team player with the ability to work discreetly, under pressure

  • Experience of working as part of a Multi-Disciplinary team

  • Flexibility to work evenings and weekends around the training schedule

  • The willingness to partake in ongoing CPD

Desirable:

  • MSc in Physiotherapy/Sports Rehabilitation/Therapy or equivalent

  • An understanding of the menstrual cycle and its effects on performance

  • Experience of working in Women’s professional football

job.title: EURO Back-Office Specialist
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: Marketing / Media Rights NTC
Contract type: Fixed-term
Start date: 01.11.2027
End date: 31.07.2028
Location: Nyon (up to one day working from home per week)
Application deadline: 13.11.2026

This role relates to UEFA EURO 2028 and is based at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland. If you are looking for roles based in the UK and Ireland, please visit the UK & Ireland 2028 Limited careers page.

Main goal

The EURO Back-Office Specialist is responsible for allocating and scheduling all confirmed services and facilities requested by broadcast partners, ensuring operational excellence, timely execution and strong collaboration across internal and external stakeholders.

Key responsibilities

  • Allocating, scheduling and processing broadcasters’ requests
  • Helping to set up the allocation and scheduling tools for unilateral services at the venues and the international broadcast centre
  • Verifying that all technical and operational requirements have been correctly planned (e.g. connectivity, resource allocation, equipment availability)
  • Liaising with other UEFA stakeholders on technical matters (engineering, production, master control room, etc.)
  • Ensuring the timely communication of updates, risks and last-minute changes
  • Producing the necessary reports to support the arbitration process
  • Producing any additional reports and layouts for the venue teams
  • Performing data quality checks for accuracy and consistency

Requirements

Experience:

  • 3–5 years of experience in a similar role

Education:

  • Bachelor's in relevant field

Languages:

  • English / Proficient

Other requirements:

- Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected

- Workflow tools, scheduling software, technical broadcast understanding

- Strong communication skills

- Ability to manage multiple priorities

- Stakeholder management

- Problem-solving and decision-making

Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.

UEFA welcomes applications from all, actively working to ensure that we are an inclusive employer that finds the best candidate for our positions, regardless of aspects such as sex, gender identification, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity or nationality.

job.title: Customer Service Assistant
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: UEFA Events SA / Ticketing
Contract type: Max-term
Location: Nyon (WFH up to one day per week)
Start date: 01/02/2027
End date: 31/07/2028

Main goal

The Customer Service Assistant (m/f/d) reports to the Customer Service Team Leader and supports the team on supervising the 1st level customer service provider and on helping the Ticketing team to improve the customer journey: pre-sale and post-sale for UEFA EURO 2028, the 2027 and 2028 club competition finals and any other event organized by UEFA.

Key responsibilities

  • Providing second-level customer service support for UEFA EURO 2028, the 2027 and 2028 UEFA club competition finals, and other events organised by UEFA (pre-sale and post-sale)
  • Helping to coordinate and supervise the first-level customer service provider (organising training, preparing presentations, quality management)
  • Helping to draft and publish content for UEFA events (website and ticket portal content, FAQs, communication support documents, email campaigns, etc.)
  • Contributing to various customer journey sub-projects, including ticket portals, mobile tickets, and payment-related topics
  • Liaising with several stakeholders linked to the customer experience, such as AccessibAll and UEFA's spectator services, safety and security, finance, and legal teams

Requirements

Experience:

  • 1 to 3 years - experience in a customer service environment, or similar
  • 1 to 3 years experience in working for sports and/or ticketing related projects is a plus

Education:

  • Bachelor's in communication, translation or similar

Languages:

  • English C2 level or English Native speaker (must-have)

Other requirements:

  • Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected
  • Knowledge of Zendesk is a plus
  • Attention to detail and structured working method

job.title: Content & CRM Specialist (Ticketing)
job.html_description:
Job information
Division/Unit: UEFA Events SA / Ticketing
Contract type: Max-term
Location: Nyon (WFH up to one day per week)
Start date: 01/02/2027
End date: 31/07/2028

Main goal

The Ticketing Content Writer & CRM Specialist is responsible for creating, editing and optimising fan-facing ticketing communications and storytelling to ensure clear and consistent messaging across UEFA EURO 2028, UEFA club competition finals and other competitions serviced by the UEFA Ticketing unit.

Key responsibilities

• Contributing to the development of UEFA's ticketing communication and storytelling strategy, ensuring fans clearly understand ticket sales processes, timelines and key updates
• Drafting and editing ticketing content for various external and internal communication channels (promotional and service email campaigns, websites, ticket sales portals, media releases, fact sheets, social media platforms etc.) in close collaboration with the communications team and other relevant stakeholders
• Ensuring that the communication strategy and terminology are applied consistently across all channels
• Identifying ticketing sales needs and planning marketing activities in accordance with the ticketing sales calendar
• Evaluating and improving marketing content and the strategy based on feedback and analysis

Requirements

Experience:

  • from 4 to 6 years as a content writer, copywriter or in a similar role, ideally in the sports industry

Languages:

  • English Native Speaker ( must-have)

Other requirements:

- Relocation to Switzerland/France is expected

- Knowledge of any other language would be an asset
- Excellent writing and communication skills
- Knowledge of the football landscape and wider sports industry would be an advantage
- Solid attention to detail

- Knowledge of any other language would be an asset - Excellent writing and communication skills - Knowledge of the football landscape and wider sports industry would be an advantage - Solid attention to detail
Want to stay updated on our latest job opportunities, events, and behind-the-scenes insights? Join us on LinkedIn.
UEFA welcomes applications from all, actively working to ensure that we are an inclusive employer that finds the best candidate for our positions, regardless of aspects such as sex, gender identification, disability, age, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity or nationality.

job.title: Goalkeeper Manager, Extended National Teams
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


Reporting directly to the Head of Goalkeeping, the Extended National Team Goalkeeper Manager will be responsible for educating, equipping, and developing our top talents through age-appropriate, skill-building approaches with the goal of grooming players to play for our Senior Extended National Teams. This role requires the implementation of coaching expertise, excellent in-person and remote communication skills, and collaboration with peers in identifying, selecting, developing, and transitioning talents through the player pathway and from other forms of the game.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Reports to the Head of Goalkeeping
  • Collaborates with the Director of Extended National Teams (Technical & Leadership), Beach, Futsal and Extended Head Coaches and Technical staff to create the best aligned environment for our players within US Soccer set structure and processes (THE U.S. WAY) Serves as the Goalkeeper Coach across Extended National Teams as needed
  •  Works to support and lead a high-performance environment for the Extended National Teams
  • Oversee the individual development and performance environment for goalkeepers 
  • Creates the conditions for an optimal on and off-the-field performance for players
  • Commits to delivering consistently to players the vision, mission, and objectives of U.S. Soccer and the overarching sporting strategy
  • Ability to align and deliver the USSF Player Development Philosophy – The U.S. WAY language (cultural anchors, performance anchors, game model, methodology, etc.)
  • Delivers the US Player pathway document outlining our areas of focus for all ages and stages of the program
  • Works collaboratively with the Talent ID department to identify, report, record, and select high potential players across the pathway
  • Contributes to the overall talent identification audit process providing outstanding player insights to support the player decision process of player selection
  • Responsible for the international development of elite Beach, Futsal and Extended players of our country
  • Ensures all national team goalkeepers within their care have an up to date and robust IDP
  • Delivers with excellence and in line with the “plan, perform, reflect, refine” model
  • Engages in the process of robust post-camp reviews with the Head of Extended National Teams (Technical & Leadership) and Head of Goalkeeping and adopts the personal development plan accordingly
  • Drives a culture of building outstanding players, staff, and club relationship
  •  Supports the US Soccer club engagement program with regular strategic club and player in-club visits
  • Upon request of the Head of Extended National Teams and Head of Goalkeeping, contribute to the US Soccer Coaching Education Programs

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • USSF “B” License or higher (or comparable UEFA B)
  • Coaching experience within elite youth development
  • Passion for working with and the developing young players 
  • Proven history of developing the individual player
  • Excellent organizational and leadership skills to manage and lead self and others
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication combined with a professional demeanor
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook) and Video Editing
  • Understands child development and maturation
  • A passion for and knowledge of talent identification
  • Possesses a growth mindset 
  • Has the ability to work as part of a wider coaching team influencing coaching within the US Soccer landscape
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, as needed
  • Willing to relocate once National Training Facility is established in Atlanta 

Desired Qualifications

  • USSF A License or equivalent
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish)
  • Coaching education experience
  • Thorough institutional knowledge of U.S. Soccer’s mission, goals, technical plan, policies, practices, and procedures   

    

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Communications
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Manager, Corporate Communications supports and executes enterprise-wide communications strategies that build understanding, strengthen relationships, create meaningful opportunities for engagement and ensure U.S. Soccer’s Federation membership base feels informed, heard and connected to the organization’s mission and direction. In close partnership with the Senior Director of Corporate Communications and business partners across the Soccer Growth and Member Strategy teams, this role is responsible for developing and executing both internal and external communications plans and initiatives that reflect U.S. Soccer’s strategic priorities and mission. 


The ideal candidate is a strategic, proactive and relationship-driven communicator with experience navigating complex stakeholder environments and aligning messaging that helps members and key stakeholders including referees, coaches and youth leaders understand how the organizations work affects them. Areas of focus include executive communications, member engagement, and cross-functional coordination. 


This role oversees the development of executive briefing materials, talking points, background documents, and presentations for public appearances, media engagements, and internal leadership communications as it relates to Soccer Growth and Member Strategy initiatives. This role also supports larger Federation external functions, including board meetings, annual member meetings, annual general meetings of member organizations, regional meetings and public-facing appearances. 


Success in this role requires strong cross-functional collaboration, the ability to synthesize complex information for diverse audiences, and a commitment to ensuring that U.S. Soccer’s internal communications infrastructure and external messaging are aligned and mission-driven. 


Primary Responsibilities 

  • Develop and execute corporate communications strategies that support organizational priorities and strengthen reputation among members, partners, media and other stakeholders. 
  • Develop executive communications, talking points, presentations, messages and other materials for internal and external audiences. 
  • Identify opportunities to proactively tell the organization’s story and demonstrate its impact. 
  • Build strong relationships across departments and serve as a communications thought partner to teams working directly with members and stakeholders. 
  • Collaborate with marketing, digital, events, executive leadership, advancement and other teams to create integrated engagement strategies. 
  • Develop and lead integrated communications strategies that strengthen member understanding, connection and engagement with the organization. 
  • Build communications plans around major organizational initiatives, changes, announcements and priorities. 
  • Play a lead role in building a monthly membership newsletter. 
  • Establish meaningful measures of communications and member engagement effectiveness. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in corporate communications, media relations, membership communications or a related field, ideally within sports, entertainment, or nonprofit sectors.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field; advanced degree a plus. 
  • Strong understanding of the U.S. soccer ecosystem, including key stakeholders such as members, referees, coaches, and youth programs. 
  • Proven experience supporting C-suite executives with briefing materials, talking points, presentations, and internal/external messaging. 
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills across a variety of formats (speeches, memos, newsletters, social content, feature articles, etc.). 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive information and craft strategic responses in high-pressure or time-sensitive situations. 
  • Experience coordinating communications for high-profile events, such as board meetings, conventions, and internal town halls. 
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Ability to develop clear, consistent messaging across internal and external channels, aligned with organizational mission and voice. 
  • Comfort working collaboratively across departments and building relationships at all levels of an organization. 
  • Experience communicating with a membership, association, nonprofit or similarly diverse stakeholder base strongly preferred.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and travel up to two times per quarter. 
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). 

Desired Qualifications 

  • Strategic hustle, initiative, and work ethic with diversity of thought. 
  • Strong posture for empathy. 
  • Ability to build meaningful relationships both internally and externally. 
  • Able to think strategically and handle multiple projects. 
  • Confidence without ego. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus, but not required. 

 

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Coordinator, Media Operations
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking a Sr. Coordinator, Media Operations to help deliver best-in-class media operations across the Federation’s 27 National Teams and major events, with a primary focus on the U.S. Men’s and Women’s National Teams.


Reporting to the Vice President, Communications, this role will be responsible for planning and executing media operations for National Team matches, camps, tournaments and other Federation events. The Sr. Coordinator will serve as a key operational contact for media and work closely with National Team press officers, Sporting, Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Commercial and venue partners to ensure media needs are thoughtfully planned and seamlessly executed.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable working in fast-paced, high-profile environments. This individual should understand the needs of working media, anticipate operational challenges and be able to independently manage multiple priorities and stakeholders while delivering a consistent, professional media experience.


The Sr. Coordinator will work cross-functionally with Communications, Sporting, Event Operations, Media, Security, Ticketing and venue partners to ensure media requirements are integrated into event planning and that U.S. Soccer delivers a consistent, professional media experience across its National Teams and events.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and execute media operations for U.S. Soccer National Team matches, camps, tournaments and Federation events, with primary focus on the Men’s and Women’s National Teams and support across all 27 National Teams as needed.
  • Manage media accreditation from application through event-day execution, including reviewing requests, assigning appropriate access, credential production and distribution, and troubleshooting accreditation issues.
  • Serve as a primary onsite point of contact for credentialed media, providing timely information, responding to questions and resolving operational issues.
  • Coordinate media facilities and operational requirements, including press boxes, media workrooms, press conference areas, mixed zones, photographer work areas and field-level positions, media entrances, connectivity, catering and other event-specific needs; manage photographer access and credential/bib distribution as required.
  • Manage media access and movement throughout venues, ensuring credentialed media are appropriately positioned, and event-specific access policies are followed.
  • Partner with venues and internal stakeholders in advance of matches and events to assess media infrastructure, determine operational needs and develop event-specific media operations plans; conduct pre-event walkthroughs and readiness checks to ensure media facilities, signage, technology and services meet established standards.
  • Partner closely with National and Youth Teams press officer to support player and coach media availability, live and virtual press conferences, training access and other team communications needs.
  • Develop and distribute media advisories and operational communications with accreditation details, schedules, access information, parking, media availability and other event logistics. Schedule virtual press conferences, provide links and meeting invites to all pertinent parties, and assist in execution.
  • Ensure U.S. Soccer Media Guidelines and event-specific access policies are consistently implemented, creating a professional working environment for journalists while protecting team needs and the rights of U.S. Soccer’s media partners.
  • Research local media markets and maintain accurate media lists and databases to support National Team and Federation communications efforts.
  • Build and maintain relationships with media operations contacts at venues, FIFA Member Associations, confederations and other soccer organizations.
  • Recruit, brief, train and manage event-day media volunteers, develop staffing plans and assignments, and establish clear roles, expectations and escalation procedures for each event.
  • Manage media operations equipment and inventory to ensure appropriate resources are available for National Team matches and events.
  • Manage media operations vendors, including sourcing services, negotiating agreements, tracking expenses and processing invoices within established budgets.
  • Collaborate with Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Ticketing, Commercial and other internal teams to ensure media requirements are incorporated into overall event planning.
  • Help develop and implement consistent media operations standards, processes and best practices across U.S. Soccer’s National Teams.
  • Support media operations planning and execution for major international tournaments and other high-profile events hosted or supported by U.S. Soccer.
  • Anticipate operational challenges and independently troubleshoot issues in real time during matches and events.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in media operations, communications, public relations, sports communications, event operations or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting media operations at major live sporting events; experience in professional or international soccer strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of media operations, accreditation and credentialing processes, venue access and the needs of working journalists, photographers and broadcasters.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage event logistics and multiple stakeholders in fast-paced, high-pressure environments.
  • Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, staffing plans, vendors and multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, solve problems and make decisions in live-event environments.
  • Strong service orientation and demonstrated ability to anticipate and respond to the needs of media and other event stakeholders.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple events, deadlines and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with media, athletes, coaches, executives, venue personnel and other high-profile stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with media accreditation, credentialing or event management platforms strongly preferred.
  • Spanish-language proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time and work nontraditional hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as needed.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

Schedule virtual press conferences, provide links and meeting invites to all pertinent parties, and assist in execution. - Ensure U.S. Soccer Media Guidelines and event-specific access policies are consistently implemented, creating a professional working environment for journalists while protecting team needs and the rights of U.S. Soccer’s media partners. - Research local media markets and maintain accurate media lists and databases to support National Team and Federation communications efforts. - Build and maintain relationships with media operations contacts at venues, FIFA Member Associations, confederations and other soccer organizations. - Recruit, brief, train and manage event-day media volunteers, develop staffing plans and assignments, and establish clear roles, expectations and escalation procedures for each event. - Manage media operations equipment and inventory to ensure appropriate resources are available for National Team matches and events. - Manage media operations vendors, including sourcing services, negotiating agreements, tracking expenses and processing invoices within established budgets. - Collaborate with Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Ticketing, Commercial and other internal teams to ensure media requirements are incorporated into overall event planning. - Help develop and implement consistent media operations standards, processes and best practices across U.S. Soccer’s National Teams. - Support media operations planning and execution for major international tournaments and other high-profile events hosted or supported by U.S. Soccer. - Anticipate operational challenges and independently troubleshoot issues in real time during matches and events.
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. - 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in media operations, communications, public relations, sports communications, event operations or a related field. - Demonstrated experience supporting media operations at major live sporting events; experience in professional or international soccer strongly preferred. - Strong understanding of media operations, accreditation and credentialing processes, venue access and the needs of working journalists, photographers and broadcasters. - Demonstrated ability to independently manage event logistics and multiple stakeholders in fast-paced, high-pressure environments. - Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, staffing plans, vendors and multiple concurrent workstreams. - Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, solve problems and make decisions in live-event environments. - Strong service orientation and demonstrated ability to anticipate and respond to the needs of media and other event stakeholders. - Exceptional organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple events, deadlines and priorities simultaneously. - Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with media, athletes, coaches, executives, venue personnel and other high-profile stakeholders. - Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with media accreditation, credentialing or event management platforms strongly preferred. - Spanish-language proficiency strongly preferred. - Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time and work nontraditional hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as needed. - General knowledge of soccer. - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments. - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
